Review Title: Spotify is a vGreat for listeners, frustrating for independent artistsery strong platform from…
Review Text:
Spotify is a very strong platform from a listener’s perspective: it is convenient, easy to use, offers a huge music library, and has become one of the main places where people discover and listen to music.

From the perspective of an independent artist, however, my experience is much more disappointing. Spotify gives the impression of reach and visibility, but in practice very little of that turns into real support or sustainable growth. Streams generate extremely low income, older achievements quickly lose visibility, follower numbers feel unstable, and without additional marketing money almost nothing happens.

The problem is not Spotify alone, but the whole system around it. Artists create the music, invest time, money and energy, while platforms, distributors, labels and marketing services benefit far more from the structure. For independent musicians, this can easily become frustrating: you keep working, hoping and investing, but the system rarely gives much back.

For listeners, Spotify is excellent. For independent artists, it can be deeply discouraging, unfair and exhausting.

Review Title: Why Am I Paying for Premium?

 However, my biggest frustration is with podcasts and the way ads are still delivered throughout episodes, even while paying for Premium.
I understand the difference between Spotify platform ads and ads embedded directly by podcast creators, but from a customer perspective, “Premium” and “ad-free” create the expectation of uninterrupted listening. Instead, podcast episodes are still constantly interrupted by host-read sponsorships and promotional segments.
 Music playback is mostly excellent, but the podcast experience feels misleading when paying customers still have to manually skip through ads and sponsored interruptions. If Spotify markets Premium as an ad-free experience, there should be clearer communication about what that actually means for podcast listeners.
 I’m not asking for perfection. I just want the uninterrupted listening experience I believed I was paying for.

Review Title: Spotify editors are changing independent artists’ genres without permission
Review Text:
I am an independent artist with multiple tracks on Spotify. I carefully submitted accurate genres via my distributor (Trap Soul, R&B/Soul, Urbano Latino etc.).
Spotify’s editorial team has systematically changed 7–9 of my tracks to completely wrong genres — mainly “American Hip Hop” and “Alternative Hip Hop”. This is not a small error. It drastically reduces my visibility in the correct playlists and audiences.
When I contacted Spotify support, they refused to provide the submitted metadata, claimed it was “algorithm + editors’ decision”, and offered no real solution. This feels like deliberate mismanagement of independent artists’ work.
Independent musicians rely on accurate genre classification for discoverability and fair streaming. Spotify’s opaque editorial system and poor support for smaller artists is a serious problem.
If you’re an independent artist, be aware that your chosen genres can be overridden with no recourse.

Review Title: I subscribed to a Premium Family plan…
Review Text:
I subscribed to a Premium Family plan on Spotify and included three users in my account. Everything was functioning normally until, without any warning or clear reason, I suddenly lost access to my account after just 13 days of use.

When I contacted support, I was informed that my account had been closed. However, no explanation was provided, and I was explicitly told that no further information could be shared. This lack of transparency is unacceptable and raises serious concerns about how user accounts are handled.

Even more concerning is the way the support process was handled. I was kept in a support chat for nearly an hour, repeatedly transferred between different agents, and ultimately left without any resolution. The case was effectively closed without addressing my concerns.

All of my playlists and years of saved music have become inaccessible due to this action. This is not just a minor service issue—it reflects a serious failure in user data access and account management responsibilities.

At this point, I intend to escalate this matter to relevant consumer protection authorities and pursue formal complaints through appropriate legal channels. I also believe this situation highlights the need for closer regulatory scrutiny of platform practices regarding account termination and user data access.

This issue should not be ignored, as it reflects a broader concern about accountability and user rights on digital platforms.
